docs.title: Extending Business Logic Across the Stack
docs.text: MODULE 2 | MODERNIZE

docs.title: EXTENDING BUSINESS LOGIC ACROSS THE STACK
i. From single-program modernization to cross-stack change
docs.text:
In the previous section, you modernized FRS409, the Order Modification Confirmation Window. Bob explained the program, converted it from fixed-format OPM RPG to free-format ILE RPG, compiled it and wrote a summary report.

Modernizing a single program is a meaningful first step, but real-world IBM i changes rarely stop at one source member. Adding a new business field, something as simple as Total Flight Hours, touches the physical file, the logical file, the RPG program and the display file. If any one of those layers is missed, the field does not appear on the screen, does not persist to the database or causes a runtime failure.

With the single-program modernization complete, this section adds a business field end to end.

Throughout the module ahead, you will first give the IBM i Developer mode a set of standing rules for fixed-column source changes. You will then use IBM Bob to explore the Flight Maintenance screen and trace the existing Mileage field through every layer. A focused impact analysis follows, after which you will add a new Total Flight Hours field across four source members. Finally, you will compile all four objects in dependency order, validate the end-to-end field mapping and confirm the result on a live 5250 terminal.

docs.title: ii. Why this matters
docs.text:
Cross-stack field changes are one of the most common, and most error-prone, activities in IBM i development.

Successfully extending a business field end to end requires more than editing one source member. Practitioners must:

  • Understand how existing fields flow from physical file through logical file, RPG program and display file
  • Identify the minimum set of source members that must change
  • Preserve DDS column alignment, field naming conventions and indicator patterns
  • Update the RPG program's F-spec record length, I-spec byte mapping, Z-ADD screen-to-file operations, O-spec output and validation subroutines
  • Compile objects in the correct dependency order (physical file, then logical file, then display file, then program)
  • Verify the result visually on a live 5250 screen
TASK WITH: Manual Change WITH: IBM Bob Premium Package for i Impact analysis DSPDBR, DSPPGMREF and a careful read of every member that opens the file A traced field path and the minimum change set, with follow-up programs listed separately DDS and fixed-column RPG edits Counting columns by hand, where a single mis-padded column means a compile failure Insert-only diffs that copy the column positions of a model line, reviewed before they are saved Standing conventions Re-explained to every developer and in every ticket Custom instructions on the mode, applied in every task Build order and validation An unwritten checklist A build in dependency order, then a validation report against the live catalog and the DDS previewer

docs.title: iii. Extending Total Flight Hours with IBM Bob
docs.text:
The goal is to add a new Total Flight Hours field to the Flight Maintenance screen, following the direct database path:

FLIGHTS.FLHRS → FLIGHTSZ.FHRS → FRS021.FHRS → FRS021DF.SFLHRS
LAYER FIELD DEFINITION Database (physical file) FLHRS 4P 0 — packed decimal, four digits, zero decimal positions Logical file and RPG FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) Screen (display file) SFLHRS Four digits, zero decimals, input/output, placed immediately after Mileage

Using IBM i Developer mode and carefully sequenced prompts, Bob can:

  • Preview the existing Flight Maintenance screen layout using the DDS Previewer
  • Trace an existing field (Mileage) end to end as a reference pattern
  • Perform a focused impact analysis identifying every affected source member
  • Propose precise, column-aligned DDS and RPG diffs for human review
  • Apply approved changes as insert-only edits, with no existing lines modified
  • Compile all four objects in dependency order with human approval at each step
  • Self-heal minor compilation errors, such as a typo in a field reference
  • Validate the completed field mapping against the live QSYS2 catalog and the DDS Previewer
ATTENTION: NON-DETERMINISTIC WORK AHEAD

Bob's responses are non-deterministic, so the exact diffs, column positions, indicator numbers and compilation messages you see may differ from those shown here.

IBM Bob is powered by generative AI and LLMs, and a defining trait of these systems is that they are non-deterministic — unlike the deterministic tools most IBM i developers are accustomed to. In practice, the same prompt can produce different DDS, RPG or display-file code from one run to the next.

All this is to say: Your results ahead may vary. The key takeaway from this workflow is that you understand how to use Bob's impact analysis, review proposed diffs and approve compilation steps. Whether or not you arrive at the exact same column positions or indicator numbers is of less importance — Bob will produce a compilable, functionally correct result either way. The exact implementation details, however, may differ from those documented here.

docs.title: iv. Creating standing rules for IBM i Developer mode
docs.text:
In fixed-column source, small alignment mistakes have large consequences. An O-spec end position padded one column to the right compiles into the wrong byte offset, and a COLHDG keyword that belongs in a physical file is an error in a display file. The prompts in this module spell out those constraints, and Bob follows them, but a constraint stated only in a prompt has to be repeated by each developer in each prompt.

The IBM Bob Premium Package for i offers a better place for them: custom instructions on the mode itself. Rules written into the IBM i Developer mode's configuration are part of Bob's context in every task that runs in that mode, without being pasted into the chat. You will add the rules for planning and implementing fixed-column code changes now, before the first edit.

THREE PLACES FOR STANDING GUIDANCE

You have now met three mechanisms that shape Bob's behavior before a prompt is read.

  1. Custom instructions on a mode travel with the mode and apply to every task that uses it.
  2. The AGENTS member written by /init travels with the library and records what Bob discovered about it.
  3. Bob Rules in a workspace's .bob/rules/ folder, which you created during the previous course, travel with the project.

Custom instructions on the mode describe how Bob should work. The AGENTS member records facts about the library. Workspace rules record facts about the project.

  1. Click the settings icon (the gear) at the top-right of the Bob panel. The Bob Settings tab opens in the editor area.

  1. Click Modes in the left sidebar of the settings tab. The table lists the built-in modes (Agent, Plan and Ask) together with the two modes the Premium Package contributes, IBM i Database and IBM i Developer, each marked with the Extension scope.

    Select IBM i Developer.

  1. The mode's detail page shows its description, its extension source (IBM i), its role definition and when to use it. Click the Edit mode (pencil) icon at the top-right of the page to open the mode editor, titled Edit IBM i Developer mode (IBM i).

  1. Scroll down through the Custom Instructions text area to the end of the existing Interaction Guidelines, and paste the following block beneath them:

    ## When a user asks to plan or implement code changes
- Make insert-only changes using apply_diff with surrounding context; do not use insert_content.
- When inserting, anchor the diff on the line ABOVE the insertion point and do not include trailing structural lines (DDS key "K ..." or record-format "R ..." lines) in the replacement - leave those lines untouched.
- When adding a fixed-form entry that mirrors an existing one (RPG I-spec, O-spec, or DDS field), copy the model line's EXACT column positions and change only the field name and value. Re-pad so numbers stay right-justified in their original columns and the data-type letter stays in its column. If the new field name is a different length than the model, adjust the padding so every downstream column is unchanged. Never eyeball the spacing.
- Preserve exact DDS column positions for field-definition entries (name, length, type). Keyword continuation lines like COLHDG only need to start after position 44 - do not fixate on their exact alignment.
- Preserve the existing OPM RPG fixed-column style.
- Do not add ALWNULL, do not use SQL ALTER TABLE, do not change the field to 5P 1.
- COLHDG belongs only in the physical file, never in the display file.
- Always show the diff and wait for my approval before saving; never compile until I say so.

    Click Save.

    READ THE RULES BEFORE YOU SAVE THEM

    Each line corresponds to a problem that came up in earlier runs of this change. The anchor above the insertion point rule keeps Bob from swallowing a DDS key line into its replacement; the copy the model line's exact columns rule keeps O-spec end positions right-justified; the never compile until I say so rule is the approval gate that the rest of this module depends on. Bob will apply them in every IBM i Developer task from now on.

  1. Close the settings tab. The prompts that follow still spell out the same constraints in full, so that the documented run can be reproduced from this page as written. In your own work, the standing rules let you shorten them considerably.

docs.title: v. Exploring the Flight Maintenance screen
docs.text:
Before changing anything, you need to understand what the Flight Maintenance screen currently looks like: which fields exist, how they are laid out and what naming conventions the display file uses.

  1. In the Bob chat panel, click the + button (top-right) and choose New task in Library List to start a fresh task scoped to your library list (QGPL, QTEMP, FLGHT400).

    Confirm that IBM i Developer is the active mode and that the Documentation and Understand permissions are enabled.

  1. Copy and paste the following prompt into the Bob chat and send it:

    Open the display file FRS021DF from FLGHT400/QDDSSRCD, show its current screen layout using the DDS Previewer, and list all the fields currently defined on the Flight Maintenance screen. Also identify: the record format used by the screen; whether each field is input, output, or input/output; the naming convention used for screen fields, including examples such as SFLGHT, SMILES, SSEATS, and SPRICE; and how visible field labels are represented in the display-file DDS. Do not modify, save, or compile anything.

    With the prompt entered, hit Enter or press the Send button to the right of the chat interface.

  1. Bob reads the display file, renders the Screen Layout (DDS Previewer — 24×80 grid) and returns a complete field inventory.

    Review the output, which includes:

    • Screen Layout: A 24×80 character grid showing the Flight Maintenance System — Flight Schedule screen with all field positions, labels and function key assignments
    • Record Format: The SELECTR format used as the main Flight Maintenance input/output screen, plus MSGRCD (message subfile) and MSGCTL (subfile control)
    • Field Inventory: Every field on the SELECTR screen — SFLGHT (Flight Number), SDYOWK (Day of the Week), SFRCTY/STOCTY (From/To City), SMILES (Mileage), SAIRLN (Airline), SST (Seats Available), SPRC (Ticket Price) and others — with line number, type, length, usage (Both, Input or Output), row and column position and description

  1. Scroll down to review the naming convention analysis.

    Bob identifies the standard IBM i DDS pattern: constants for labels and named fields for data. Labels are quoted string constants on a name-less DDS line, and the data entry field is defined on the next line, positioned a few columns to the right. Labels are colored blue (COLOR(BLU)), while data fields may carry DSPATR(HI) or DSPATR(RI) for error highlighting.

docs.title: vi. Performing a focused impact analysis
docs.text:
With the screen layout understood, the next step is to trace how an existing field flows through the full stack, and then identify which source members must change to add a new one.

  1. Within the Agentic Sidebar chat, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    Perform a focused impact analysis for adding Total Flight Hours to the Flight Maintenance application in FLGHT400. Use these requirements: add database field FLHRS; expose it to RPG as FHRS; display it on the screen as SFLHRS; use four numeric digits with zero decimal positions; place it immediately after Mileage on the Flight Maintenance screen. First, trace the existing Mileage field through the application. Show how the database field in FLIGHTS is exposed through FLIGHTSZ, handled by FRS021, and displayed as SMILES in FRS021DF. Then identify the minimum source members that must change to implement Total Flight Hours in the direct Flight Maintenance path. Confirm: whether FLIGHTS is defined by DDS; whether FLIGHTSZ explicitly lists and renames fields; how FRS021 defines the FLIGHTSZ record layout; how FRS021 maps database values to screen values; which objects must be rebuilt or recompiled. Mention any additional affected programs as follow-up work, but do not analyze or modify those programs during this demonstration. Do not modify, save, or compile anything.

    HOW THE UNDERSTAND SCAN HELPS

    With the Understand permission enabled, Bob can take the list of programs that open FLIGHTS and FLIGHTSZ from the scan rather than searching source members for file names. This is how Bob lists the follow-up programs at the end of the analysis without opening each of them.

    Bob reads all four source members and produces Confirmed Answers to Each Question:

    • Is FLIGHTS defined by DDS? — Yes. FLIGHTS.PF is a DDS Physical File in FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF with 11 database fields, including MILEAGE (9B 0, ALWNULL, COLHDG('MILEAGE'))
    • Does FLIGHTSZ explicitly list and rename every field? — Yes. FLIGHTSZ.LF is a DDS Logical File whose sole purpose is to rename every field from truncated physical-file names into meaningful short names using RENAME. All 11 fields are explicitly enumerated — adding a new field to FLIGHTS will NOT automatically appear in FLIGHTSZ; it must be added manually
    • How does FRS021 define the FLIGHTSZ record layout? — FRS021.RPG is OPM RPG/400. It uses a program-described (rather than externally described) file declaration for FLIGHTSZ with a hardcoded record length (233 bytes) and byte-mapped I-spec fields
    • How does FRS021 map database values to screen values? — Explicit Z-ADD / MOVE operations in subroutine @F10SR (write) and via the FRS413 PARM return (read and lookup)

  1. Bob produces a Complete Mileage Field Trace (End-to-End) as a Mermaid diagram, showing the full path from FLIGHTS.PF (MILEAGE 9B 0) through FLIGHTSZ.LF (MILES RENAME(MILEAGE)) to FRS021.RPG (FMILES I-spec, Z-ADD to SMILES) to FRS021DF.DSPF (SMILES 5D 0B on row 15) and into the validation subroutine @ERRCK.

  1. Bob identifies the Minimum Source Members to Change — Direct Flight Maintenance Path Only. Four source members must change; nothing else is required for the core FRS021 path to work end to end:

    # SOURCE MEMBER LIBRARY / FILE WHAT MUST CHANGE 1 FLIGHTS.PF FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF Add new field FLHRS after MILEAGE, with a COLHDG 2 FLIGHTSZ.LF FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF Add FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) after MILES 3 FRS021.RPG FLGHT400/QRPGSRC Update the F-spec record length; add the I-spec for FHRS; add Z-ADD operations; add validation; add O-spec entries 4 FRS021DF.DSPF FLGHT400/QDDSSRCD Add a label constant and the field SFLHRS with CHECK(RZ), plus conditional DSPATR(RI) and DSPATR(PC) on a free indicator

  1. Bob provides the Build / Recompile Order (objects must be rebuilt in this sequence because of the dependency chain) and identifies Follow-Up Work — Additional Affected Programs (Not Analysed Here): FRS413.RPG, FRS001.RPG, FRS002.RPG and BFLGHT.RPG, all of which open FLIGHTSZ with a hardcoded 233-byte record length.

    1. CRTPF   FLIGHTS     ← must be rebuilt first (schema change)
2. CRTLF   FLIGHTSZ    ← depends on FLIGHTS
3. CRTRPGPGM FRS021    ← depends on FLIGHTSZ record length & FMILES position
4. CRTDSPF FRS021DF    ← screen layout, compiled independently
   (FRS021 must be recompiled after FRS021DF if display file changes)

  1. Review the Summary table that consolidates all findings from the impact analysis:

    QUESTION ANSWER Is FLIGHTS defined by DDS? Yes — FLIGHTS.PF in FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF Does FLIGHTSZ explicitly list fields? Yes — all 11 fields are RENAMEd; new fields must be added manually How does FRS021 define the FLIGHTSZ layout? Program-described F-spec, 233-byte record, byte-mapped I-spec fields How are database values mapped to screen values? Explicit Z-ADD / MOVE operations in subroutine @F10SR (write) and via the FRS413 PARM return (read and lookup) Minimum members to change 4: FLIGHTS.PF, FLIGHTSZ.LF, FRS021.RPG, FRS021DF.DSPF Objects to rebuild 4 objects in dependency order: FLIGHTS → FLIGHTSZ → FRS021DF → FRS021 Follow-up programs FRS413, FRS001, FRS002, BFLGHT — to be reviewed and recompiled in a later change

    REVIEW THE ANALYSIS BEFORE ANYTHING IS EDITED

    Everything after this point executes the plan. Before moving on, confirm four things in the analysis:

    • It touches only the four demo objects
    • It names the fields FLHRS, FHRS and SFLHRS correctly
    • It includes the record-length change for the 3-byte packed field
    • It lists every other program as follow-up only

    The plan stays in the chat, which Bob keeps in context for the prompts that follow.

docs.title: vii. Updating the DDS source
docs.text:
With the impact analysis complete and reviewed, the next step is to update the two DDS source members: the physical file and the logical file.

Sub-Task 1: Update FLIGHTS.PF and FLIGHTSZ.LF

Bob proposes insert-only changes to both DDS source members. No existing lines are modified. The new field FLHRS is added after MILEAGE in the physical file, and FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) is added after MILES in the logical file. Both changes preserve the exact column alignment of their neighboring DDS lines.

  1. Within the Agentic Sidebar chat, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    Update the DDS source for the direct database path: In FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF(FLIGHTS), add FLHRS as a packed-decimal field with four digits and zero decimal positions. Add an appropriate COLHDG consistent with the existing physical-file DDS. In FLGHT400/QDDSSRCF(FLIGHTSZ), add FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) so the new physical-file field is available to the RPG program. Preserve the exact column positions of all existing DDS lines; make insert-only changes. Do not add ALWNULL, do not change the field to 5P 1, and do not use SQL ALTER TABLE. Show the proposed diffs. Do not save or compile anything until I review them.

  1. Bob produces Proposed Diffs (read-only — do not apply until you approve).

    Diff 1 — FLIGHTS.PF

    Insert two new lines after line 52 (after COLHDG('MILEAGE')), before the key spec on line 53. The new field FLHRS matches the column alignment of MILEAGE in full:

    • FLHRS starts at column 20 (matching MILEAGE)
    • 4P 0 starts at column 30 (matching the 9B 0 of MILEAGE)
    • COLHDG('FLIGHT_HOURS') starts at column 46 (matching COLHDG('MILEAGE'))

    Diff 2 — FLIGHTSZ.LF

    Insert one new line after line 13 (after MILES RENAME(MILEAGE)), before the key spec on line 14. The new line matches the column layout of all other RENAME lines:

    • A at column 6 (standard DDS form type)
    • FHRS at column 15 (the field name position, matching MILES, SEATS, TKTPR and the rest)
    • RENAME(FLHRS) at column 45 (matching all other RENAME keywords on existing lines)

    Review the Summary of Changes table confirming that both changes are insert-only, with no ALWNULL, no 5P 1 and no SQL.

    • Once satisfied, copy & paste the following instruction into the Agentic Sidebar
    • Press Enter to execute the task
    I approve these two DDS source changes. Save both source members, but do not compile them yet.

  1. Bob applies both inserts, verifies the final state of each member and confirms:

    • FLIGHTS.PF — saved ✓: Line 53 (new): FLHRS 4P 0 — packed decimal, 4 digits, 0 decimal positions; field name at column 20 and type at column 30, matching the MILEAGE column alignment. Line 54 (new): COLHDG('FLIGHT_HOURS') — column heading at column 46, matching all other COLHDG lines in the file. All 53 original lines are untouched; K FLIGH00001 is now line 55
    • FLIGHTSZ.LF — saved ✓: Line 14 (new): A FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) — A at column 6, FHRS at column 15 and RENAME(FLHRS) at column 45, matching every other RENAME line in the file. All 14 original lines are untouched; K FLGHTN is now line 15

docs.title: viii. Updating the display file
docs.text:
Sub-Task 2: Update FRS021DF.DSPF

Bob proposes a six-line insert into the display file: a label constant, a COLOR(BLU) attribute, the SFLHRS data field with CHECK(RZ), and conditional DSPATR(RI) / DSPATR(PC) attributes on an available indicator. The new field is placed on row 16, immediately after Mileage on row 15 and before the Airline label on row 17.

  1. Within the Agentic Sidebar chat, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    Update FLGHT400/QDDSSRCD(FRS021DF) to add an input/output screen field named SFLHRS for Total Flight Hours. Requirements: four numeric digits; zero decimal positions; positioned immediately after Mileage; visible label: Flight Hours; use CHECK(RZ) to match the comparable numeric fields on this screen; preserve the existing display-file DDS style. Do not add COLHDG — it is not valid in a display file. Ensure that the label and field fit within the screen and do not overlap existing fields, message areas, or function-key text. Show the proposed diff and updated DDS preview. Do not save or compile anything until I review it.

    Bob checks indicator usage (51 to 60 are already used) and selects the next available indicator (61). It produces a Proposed Diff — FRS021DF.DSPF: insert six lines after line 104 (after the last DSPATR line belonging to SMILES), before the Airline label on line 105. No existing lines are changed.

  1. Bob renders an Updated Screen Layout Preview (24×80) showing the new field in context:

    Row 15 | Mileage. . . . . . . . . .   [SMILES ]    ← row 15, col 35, 5 digits
Row 16 | Flight Hours . . . . . . .   [FLHRS ]     ← NEW row 16, col 37, 4 digits
Row 17 | Airline. . . . . .           [SAIRLN ]    ( F8 to Select )

    Bob confirms No overlaps: row 16 columns 2 to 35 (the label) are clear; row 16 columns 37 to 40 (SFLHRS, four digits) end at column 40, well inside the right margin; SMILES on row 15 and SFLHRS on row 16 are on different rows with no conflict; the Airline label on row 17 is unchanged.

  1. Once you have reviewed the proposed diff and screen preview, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    I approve the display-file change. Save FRS021DF, but do not compile it yet.

  1. Bob saves the display file and confirms what was written:

    • FRS021DF.DSPF — saved correctly — six lines inserted at lines 105 to 110, all surrounding lines undisturbed
    • Three source members are now updated and saved, none compiled yet: FLIGHTS.PF ✓, FLIGHTSZ.LF ✓, FRS021DF.DSPF ✓
    • Next up: FRS021.RPG — four targeted changes needed (F-spec, I-spec, validation, and the Z-ADD and O-spec additions)

docs.title: ix. Updating the RPG program
docs.text:
Sub-Task 3: Update FRS021.RPG

Bob proposes targeted changes to the RPG program to handle the new field: updating the F-spec record length, adding an I-spec byte mapping, inserting Z-ADD operations in the ADD, UPDATE and ELSE branches, adding O-spec entries for both exception output groups and adding a validation block in the @ERRCK subroutine. All changes follow the existing Mileage implementation as the pattern.

  1. Within the Agentic Sidebar chat, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    Update FLGHT400/QRPGSRC(FRS021) to handle Total Flight Hours using the existing Mileage implementation as the pattern. Make the minimum changes needed to: increase the program-described FLIGHTSZ record length for the new packed field; add FHRS to the input specification at the correct record positions; load SFLHRS from FHRS when an existing record is retrieved; move SFLHRS to FHRS during add and update processing; include FHRS in the add and update output specifications; validate the screen value consistently with the existing numeric screen fields. Preserve the existing OPM RPG style and fixed-column positioning. After every successful CHAIN used to load an existing flight for display, explicitly move FHRS to SFLHRS, following the same database-to-screen pattern used for Mileage. Do not assume that the display file maps FHRS to SFLHRS automatically. Do not modify any other programs during this demonstration. Show the proposed diff and explain each change briefly. Do not save or compile anything until I review it.
    ALIGNMENT TROUBLE? SPLIT THE RPG CHANGE INTO THREE DIFFS

    FRS021 is fixed-form OPM RPG and the most alignment-sensitive member in this change. If Bob's single diff mis-pads a column, or if you prefer smaller approvals, ask for the change in three parts instead and approve each before the next. Do not compile at any of the three steps.

    F-spec and I-spec (record length plus the packed input field):

    Apply just the F-spec and I-spec changes to FLGHT400/QRPGSRC(FRS021): increase the FLIGHTSZ record length from 233 to 236, and add the FHRS input-spec entry at positions 234-236 using data-type P (packed) in column 43, mirroring the exact column alignment of the neighboring FMILES entry. Show the diff and wait for my approval; do not compile.

    C-specs (screen-to-database moves and validation):

    Now apply just the C-spec changes to FRS021: after every successful CHAIN that loads an existing flight, move FHRS to SFLHRS; move SFLHRS to FHRS on both the add and update paths (mirroring the existing Z-ADD SMILES/FMILES lines); and add an SFLHRS validation consistent with the SMILES check using the next free indicator. Show the diff and wait for my approval; do not compile.

    O-specs (the alignment-sensitive part):

    Finally apply just the O-spec changes to FRS021: add FHRS to both the ADDFLT and UPDFLT output records. Copy the exact column positions of the neighboring FMILES O-spec line and change only the field name and end position — the end position must stay right-justified in the same columns, with the packed data-type letter in the same column as FMILES's B. Do not eyeball the spacing. Show the diff and wait for my approval; do not compile.

    OPM RPG O-spec end positions are column-sensitive. If Bob mis-pads, the compiler reads the wrong end position (238 instead of 236, say) and fails. Verify that the end position of FHRS lines up in the same columns as the 233 of FMILES before approving. FHRS is packed (4P 0, three bytes), so its I-spec carries P in the data-type column; the neighboring FMILES is binary and carries B.

  1. Bob produces a Proposed Diff — FRS021.RPG with the following changes:

    Change 1 — F-spec: record length 233 → 236: The F-spec line for FFLIGHTSZUF is updated from 233 to 236. FFHRS is 4P 0, which is three bytes, appended after FMILES (bytes 230 to 233). The new total is 236.

    Change 2 — I-spec: add FFHRS P 234–236 0 after FMILES: A new I-spec line maps the new packed-decimal bytes 234 to 236 to the RPG field FFHRS, four digits and zero decimals.

    Change 3 — @ERRCK: validate SFLHRS after the SMILES block: A validation block for SFLHRS using indicator 61 and message FRS0025, following the same SETON/MOVE/EXSR/GOTO pattern.

  1. Scroll down to review the remaining changes:

    Change 4 — ADD branch: Z-ADDSFLHRS FFHRS — screen to file before EXCPTADDFLT

    Change 5 — ELSE (UPDATE) branch: Z-ADDFFHRS SFLHRS — database to screen load after CHAIN

    Change 6 — UPDATE branch: Z-ADDSFLHRS FFHRS — screen to file before EXCPTUPDFLT

    Change 7 — O-specs: FFHRS 236P in both the ADDFLT and UPDFLT exception output groups

    Once you have reviewed all proposed changes and are satisfied they are correct, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    I approve the FRS021 changes. Save the source member, but do not compile yet.

  1. Bob applies all seven changes in a single apply_diff call, verifies each against the saved source and confirms with a change-by-change verification table:

    # LINE(S) CHANGE VERIFIED 1 4 F-spec: 233 → 236 — accommodates the 3-byte packed FFHRS appended after FMILES ✓ 2 23 I-spec: P 234 236 0 FFHRS — maps packed bytes 234 to 236 to the RPG field FFHRS ✓ 3 326–331 @ERRCK: SFLHRS IFEQ *ZEROS validation block, indicator 61, message FRS0025 ✓ 4 524 ADD branch: Z-ADDSFLHRS FFHRS — screen to file before EXCPTADDFLT ✓ 5 529 ELSE (UPDATE) branch: Z-ADDFFHRS SFLHRS — explicit database-to-screen load after CHAIN ✓ 6 570 UPDATE branch: Z-ADDSFLHRS FFHRS — screen to file before EXCPTUPDFLT ✓ 7 610 O-spec ADDFLT: FFHRS 236P — writes packed bytes 234 to 236 on add ✓ 8 624 O-spec UPDFLT: FFHRS 236P — writes packed bytes 234 to 236 on update ✓

    All four source members are now saved, none compiled:

    MEMBER STATUS FLIGHTS.PF ✓ FLHRS 4P 0 + COLHDG('FLIGHT_HOURS') added FLIGHTSZ.LF ✓ FHRS RENAME(FLHRS) added FRS021DF.DSPF ✓ SFLHRS 4D 0B at row 16, indicator 61 FRS021.RPG ✓ F-spec, I-spec, validation, load, store, O-specs

docs.title: x. Compiling all four objects
docs.text:
Sub-Task 4: Build the Direct Flight Maintenance Path

Bob compiles all four objects in dependency order: CHGPF FLIGHTS → CRTLF FLIGHTSZ → CRTDSPF FRS021DF → CRTRPGPGM FRS021. Each step requires your approval. Bob will stop on any compilation failure and report the error for your review.

  1. Within the Agentic Sidebar chat, copy & paste the following instruction. Press Enter to execute the task.

    Build only the direct Flight Maintenance path in this order: 1. Apply the updated DDS for FLGHT400/FLIGHTS 2. Rebuild FLGHT400/FLIGHTSZ 3. Compile FLGHT400/FRS021DF 4. Compile FLGHT400/FRS021. Use the correct IBM i command for each source type. Stop if one of these four objects fails — report the compile error briefly and wait for my direction. Do not modify or compile unrelated programs. List additional impacted programs as follow-up work only.

  1. Bob generates a Todo List with four steps and pauses for approval:

    TODO LIST

    • Step 1: Apply updated DDS — CHGPF FLGHT400/FLIGHTS
    • Step 2: Rebuild logical file — CRTLF FLGHT400/FLIGHTSZ
    • Step 3: Compile display file — CRTDSPF FLGHT400/FRS021DF
    • Step 4: Compile RPG program — CRTRPGPGM FLGHT400/FRS021

    Click Approve todo tools for task to let Bob execute all four build steps.

    WHY CHGPF RATHER THAN CRTPF

    The impact analysis listed CRTPF for the physical file. When Bob comes to build, it chooses CHGPF. CHGPF applies the new DDS to the existing file in place and preserves the records it holds, whereas CRTPF would require the file to be deleted and recreated. The build summary confirms how many records survived the change.

  1. Bob completes all four steps and produces a Build Complete — Direct Flight Maintenance Path summary:

    STEP OBJECT COMMAND RESULT 1 FLIGHTS *FILE PF CHGPF ✅ Changed in place — 482,332 records preserved. FLHRS 4P 0 at buffer position 229 2 FLIGHTSZ *FILE LF DLTF + CRTLF ✅ Rebuilt clean — FHRS 4P 0B at buffer position 234 3 FRS021DF *FILE DSPF CRTDSPF REPLACE(*YES) ✅ Zero errors — SFLHRS 4D 0B at row 16, column 37 4 FRS021 *PGM CRTRPGPGM REPLACE(*YES) ✅ Highest severity 00 — one typo corrected mid-build (FHRS → FFHRS)

    Bob notes the one fix applied during compilation: on line 529 of FRS021.RPG, Z-ADDFHRS was corrected to Z-ADDFFHRS. The I-spec field is named FFHRS, and the C-spec had the F prefix missing.

    TROUBLESHOOTING: A COMPILE FAILS

    If one of the four objects fails to compile, keep Bob scoped to the four objects: "Explain the direct cause and propose the smallest correction limited to the four demo objects. Do not modify anything yet." If the cause is an OPM RPG column-alignment issue, remind Bob to copy the model line's exact columns rather than counting by eye. If a program such as FRS003, FRS413 or BFLGHT is also affected, record it as follow-up work; do not update or compile it here.

    • ✅ Check 1 — FLHRS exists in FLGHT400/FLIGHTS: FLHRS DECIMAL, 4 digits, 0 decimals, NOT NULL, ordinal position 13. Confirmed via QSYS2.SYSCOLUMNS. FLHRS is the 13th column, immediately after MILEAGE (position 12). Not nullable, since no ALWNULL was added, as required. The data type is DECIMAL, the SQL representation of 4P 0 packed decimal

    The field is positioned at row 16, column 37, where the DDS Previewer showed it. The label reads Flight Hours . . . . . . . in the same dot-leader style as Mileage, Seats Available and Ticket Price.
