docs.title: Generating a React Carbon App from a Green Screen
docs.text: MODULE 6 | EXTEND (OPTIONAL)

docs.title: GENERATING A REACT CARBON APP FROM A GREEN SCREEN
i. From the green screen to the browser
docs.text:
The five required modules are complete, and the accreditation instructions in Module 5 are where the course formally ends. This optional module is for the participant with time and token budget to spare, and it covers the one layer the earlier modules did not touch: the user interface.

Every screen in FLIGHT400 is a 5250 display file. The Create Order screen (FRS001DF, driven by FRS001) is a good example: two boxed panels of flight and ticket information, a row of function keys along the bottom and a set of fields whose valid values live in lookup programs reached with F4 through F7. Its business logic is sound. Clients usually raise modernization because of the 5250 interface.

Throughout this module, you will give Bob a helper skill that captures how to build and run a React and Vite application inside IBM i PASE, then switch to IBM i Developer mode and ask Bob to generate a single-page React application styled with IBM Carbon from a screenshot of the 5250 screen. Bob reads the display file and the RPG program behind it, scaffolds the project in the IFS, builds it on the partition and starts its development server there. You open the result in your own browser through an SSH tunnel.

THIS MODULE IS OPTIONAL

Expect about 30 minutes, most of it spent waiting for npm install to finish on the partition. The module installs Node.js in PASE if it is not already present, which is a change to the partition beyond the FLGHT400 library. Nothing here is required for accreditation.

docs.title: ii. Why this matters
docs.text:
A modern front end is the most visible modernization outcome. On IBM i it is often handed to an outside team, because the toolchain is unfamiliar to RPG developers.

Building a web front end for a 5250 transaction by hand requires engineers to:

  • Read the display file DDS and the RPG program to learn which fields exist, which are input and which carry lookups
  • Know the quirks of running Node.js, npm and a bundler inside PASE on a big-endian POWER system
  • Choose and configure a design system so that the result looks like an enterprise application rather than a prototype
  • Keep the development server running in the background without tying up the session that started it
  • Reach the server from a developer's laptop through whatever network path the partition allows
TASK WITH: Manual Development WITH: IBM Bob Premium Package for i Understanding the screen Reading FRS001DF and FRS001 by hand The dds-primer-basics and rpg-primer-basics skills parse the layout, fields and pricing logic PASE toolchain pitfalls Discovered one failed build at a time Recorded in a helper skill that Bob applies on each run Scaffolding and styling Hours of boilerplate and Carbon configuration A generated project with the theme, components and launch scripts in place Running on the partition Shell scripts written by hand Start and stop on request, with the server detached from the chat session

docs.title: iii. Extending FLIGHT400 with IBM Bob
docs.text:
The work in this module combines three things you have already used (a skill, the IBM i Developer mode and Bob's IFS and PASE tools) with one you author yourself. The skill is the new element. React and Vite run well inside PASE, but only once a handful of platform-specific problems are solved:

  • The native esbuild binary does not exist for os400
  • npm postinstall scripts hang
  • An interactive scaffolding prompt freezes the tool channel
  • nohup npm run dev & leaves a pipe open that cancels the call

A skill records those solutions so that Bob applies them without being told.

Using IBM i Developer mode with the helper skill in place, Bob can:

  • Read FRS001DF.DSPF for the screen layout and field names, and FRS001.RPG for the pricing logic and field definitions
  • Scaffold a React 18 and Vite 4 project in the IFS and install its dependencies with npm
  • Patch esbuild for os400 and configure Vite and Sass for the Carbon theme
  • Write the launch scripts and start the development server in the background on a port you choose
  • Stop the server again when you are done

ATTENTION: NON-DETERMINISTIC WORK AHEAD

Bob's responses are non-deterministic, and this module asks Bob to design a user interface, which leaves more room for variation than any earlier prompt. The layout, component choices and lookup values you see will differ from the screenshot, and the build may need a second attempt if a step of the skill is skipped.

All this is to say: Your results ahead may vary. The key takeaway is that you understand how to capture platform knowledge in a skill, how Bob combines it with the Premium Package's own skills to read a 5250 screen, and how a generated application is built and run on the partition. Whether your page matches the one shown is of less importance than the fact that it renders the Create Order screen in a browser.

PREREQUISITES

  • The SSH private key from Setup is still in your local workspace folder, and an SSH client is available in the Bob IDE's integrated terminal
  • Port 3001 is free on your laptop (the tunnel binds it) and on the partition (the development server binds it)
  • The IBM i Modernization connection is active and FLGHT400 is on the library list

docs.title: iv. Preparing Node.js on the partition
docs.text:
The Certified PowerVS Base VM ships without Node.js. As with tn5250 during Setup, you will have Bob install it rather than doing so by hand. PASE packages come from yum, and the Node.js packages are versioned (nodejs20, nodejs22 and so on) rather than published under a generic name.

  1. In the Bob chat panel, confirm that IBM i Developer is the active mode, click + › New task in Library List and send the following prompt:

    Check whether Node.js and npm are installed in PASE on this partition by running /QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/node --version and /QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/npm --version. If Node.js is missing, list the nodejs packages available from yum, install the newest version that is 18 or later (for example yum install nodejs22), and report both versions when done.

    Approve the PASE command requests as they appear. The install takes a few minutes and ends with Bob reporting a Node.js version of 18 or later and an npm version of 9 or later.

    WHY THE FULL PATH

    PASE shells do not add /QOpenSys/pkgs/bin to the PATH automatically, so node on its own reports No such file or directory even when Node.js is installed. The helper skill you create next tells Bob to use the fully qualified path everywhere and to export the PATH at the top of every script it writes, which avoids a whole class of confusing failures.

docs.title: v. Creating the helper skill
docs.text:
A skill is a Markdown file with a short frontmatter (a name and a description that tells Bob when to apply it) followed by the instructions themselves. You met the Premium Package's own skills in Module 1, when understand-app-overview answered a question from the scan. You create this one yourself. Its text is provided with the lab; you will paste it into a chat and ask Bob to turn it into a skill.

  1. Open the skill text: ibmi-react-vite-SKILL.txt. Save it into your local workspace folder (~/ibmiflight400) or open it in the Bob IDE's editor, then select its entire content and copy it.

    WHAT THE SKILL ENCODES

    Read it before you paste it; it is a compact account of what goes wrong when a toolchain written for Linux runs in PASE. It tells Bob to:

    • Gather the screen name, target path, theme and port before writing a file
    • Scaffold non-interactively
    • Install with npm install --ignore-scripts
    • Patch esbuild/lib/main.js so that Vite falls back to esbuild-wasm on os400
    • Declare the Carbon theme before the component styles and wrap the app in <Theme>
    • Start the development server through a start-dev.sh launcher that resolves its environment before forking, rather than through nohup npm run dev &

    Each rule prevents a failure that occurred in earlier builds.

  1. In the Bob chat panel, switch the mode selector to Agent. Click + and choose Local Workspace (your ibmiflight400 folder) as the task context. Paste the copied skill text into the prompt, append the following instruction on a new line and send it:

    Create a skill from the pasted text.

    Bob writes the skill file and confirms where it saved it. If Bob asks whether to save the skill globally or in the workspace, choose global, so that it is available from the library-list task in the next section.

docs.title: vi. Generating the React application
docs.text:
With Node.js in place and the skill saved, the generation itself is a single prompt with an image attached. The image is a screenshot of the 5250 Create Order screen; the Premium Package's dds-primer-basics and rpg-primer-basics skills do the rest of the reading from the display file and the program.

  1. Save the screenshot of the Create Order screen to your laptop: ppi-create-order-screen.png (right-click the image and save it). If you prefer your own capture, sign on to the 5250 terminal, start the application with GO FLGHT400/FRSMAIN and take a screenshot of the order entry screen.

  1. Switch the mode selector back to IBM i Developer. Click + › New task in Library List so that the task is scoped to FLGHT400, and confirm in the Permissions menu that Documentation and Understand are enabled.

  1. Drag the screenshot into the prompt field (or paste it from the clipboard), then paste the following prompt beneath it and send it:

    Given this screenshot of the 5250 flight order screen from the application FLIGHT400 in @FLGHT400, build a single-page React 18 + Vite 4 app on IBM i (PASE) using @carbon/react ^1.x with the g100 dark theme that modernises the IBM i 5250 screen shown in the attached screenshot. Create the app in the IFS at $HOME/flight400-frontend-apps/create-order/. Use the g100 dark theme. All fields should have a list of values to select from. The dev server must run in the background using nohup ... & and write output to /tmp/vite-dev.log. Pin the Vite dev server to port 3001 if available.

    THE @ MENTION

    @FLGHT400 attaches the library to the task's context, which is how Bob knows where to find FRS001DF and FRS001 without being told their source files. Type the @ and pick the library from the list that appears, so that it is highlighted as a mention rather than left as plain text.

  1. Bob drafts a to-do list and pauses for approval. In the documented run, it activated the ibmi-react-vite skill together with dds-primer-basics (to parse FRS001DF.DSPF for the layout, field names and subfile windows) and rpg-primer-basics (to read FRS001.RPG for the pricing logic and field definitions), then listed the steps of the skill: scaffold, write package.json, install, patch esbuild, configure Vite and the theme, write the components and the launch scripts, and build.

    Click Approve todo tools for task, then approve the PASE command and IFS write requests as they appear. The npm install step is the long one; expect the whole task to take ten to fifteen minutes.

    TROUBLESHOOTING: THE BUILD FAILS

    Most failures trace back to a step of the skill being skipped. Unsupported platform: os400 ppc64 BE means the esbuild patch did not run; ask Bob to re-run node patch-esbuild.cjs and build again. A hang during npm install means --ignore-scripts was omitted. A page that renders in the white theme means the theme @use landed after the component styles. In each case, point Bob to the relevant section of the skill instead of describing the fix, since the skill already contains it.

  1. When the build completes, ask Bob to start the server:

    Please start the dev server for the app you just created.

    Bob runs the start-dev.sh launcher, which detaches the Vite server with nohup and records its process ID. It reports the PID and the port the server is listening on. If port 3001 was taken, Vite moves to the next free port and Bob tells you which; use that port in the tunnel below.

docs.title: vii. Opening the application from your laptop
docs.text:
The development server listens on the partition, and the partition's public interface does not expose port 3001. An SSH tunnel carries the port to your laptop over the same connection Bob uses.

  1. In the Bob IDE, open a local terminal (Terminal → New Terminal) at the root of your workspace, where ssh_private_key.pem lives. Run the following, replacing <public-ip> with the Virtual machine 1 public IP address from your TechZone reservation, and leave the terminal open:

    ssh -i ssh_private_key.pem -N -L 3001:localhost:3001 ITZUSER@<public-ip>

    -N opens the tunnel without starting a remote shell, so the command appears to hang. The command is holding the tunnel open, which is expected. Press Ctrl+C to close it when you are finished.

  1. Open http://localhost:3001 in your browser. The Create Order screen renders as a Carbon page in the g100 dark theme, with the Flight Information and Ticket Order Information panels as tiles. The lookups become dropdowns and the class of service becomes a set of radio buttons. The function keys appear as a row of buttons along the bottom, with F10 – Make Reservation as the primary action.

    TROUBLESHOOTING: NOTHING SHOWING IN THE BROWSER

    Check three things in order. The tunnel terminal is still open and reported no error. The port in the tunnel matches the port Bob reported in the previous section; if Vite moved to another port, change both ends of the -L argument. And the server is still running: ask Bob "Is the dev server for the create-order app still running? Show the last lines of its log." The log is at /tmp/vite-create-order.log (the skill names it after the screen) or at /tmp/vite-dev.log.

  1. When you have finished exploring, ask Bob to stop the server:

    Stop the web service for FLIGHT400 on port 3001.

    Bob reads the recorded PID and ends the process. Close the tunnel with Ctrl+C in the terminal. A Node.js server left running would show up as a PASE job in the active-jobs list from Module 5, which is a useful check if you are unsure whether it stopped.

    SAMPLE DATA ONLY

    The generated application runs with sample data; its dropdowns are populated from what Bob read in the display file and the RPG program, and Make Reservation does not write an order. The natural next step is a REST layer that connects the page to the real business logic and to Db2 for i. FLIGHT400 already has the beginnings of one: the six ILE service programs that the Understand scan reported in Module 1 are its REST API layer, and the AGENTS member records how they must be compiled.

docs.title: viii. Key takeaways
docs.text:
• A skill you author yourself works the same way as the Premium Package's own: a Markdown file with a description that tells Bob when to apply it, which Bob then combines with the platform skills (dds-primer-basics, rpg-primer-basics) that a task needs
  • Platform knowledge belongs in a skill. The esbuild patch, --ignore-scripts, the non-interactive scaffold and the detached launcher are recorded there and applied on each run
  • Bob can read a 5250 screen from its DDS and its RPG program and produce a React application styled with IBM Carbon that preserves the fields, lookups and function keys of the original
  • The application is built and served on the partition itself, in PASE, and reached from a laptop through an SSH tunnel; only the browser runs outside the IBM i
  • A generated front end on sample data is a starting point; connecting it to the application's REST layer and to Db2 for i is the modernization work that follows
  • Human review remains essential. A page that renders is a prototype; compare the generated fields and lookups with the display file before it is shown as finished work

This concludes the optional module and the IBM Bob Premium Package for i Hands-on lab. If you have not yet done so, return to the accreditation instructions in Module 5 to record your Stand & Deliver or complete the skills evaluation quiz.

docs.title: Registration and Setup
docs.text: GETTING STARTED

docs.title: REGISTRATION AND SETUP
i. Before you begin
docs.text:
Christopher Bienko (AI Enablement GTM Product Manager) provides an overview of the Registration and Setup module for the hands-on enablement. [1 min]

Before you begin the hands-on modules, complete the registration and setup steps below. By the end you will have an authenticated IBM Bob account entitled to the IBM Bob Premium Package for i (PPi), and an IBM i 7.6 partition that holds the Flight400 demo application used in every module.

The hands-on work ahead assumes you have completed the core curriculum of the Climbing the AI Maturity Curve L3 course, or that you hold equivalent familiarity with the Bob IDE and the Agentic Sidebar as well as Rules and AGENTS.md. No prior IBM i experience is required: the Setup chapter provisions the partition for you, and the modules explain each IBM i concept where it first appears.

What you do need:

LAB PREREQUISITES

  • IBM Bob installed and authenticated on your local machine
  • Your IBMid credentials are at hand (IBM regular employees sign in with their w3id)
  • IBM regular employees: access to the w3 add-ons portal to request the Premium Package for i entitlement
  • Business Partners: access to IBM Technology Zone to request the Premium Package for i entitlement
  • Access to IBM Technology Zone to reserve an IBM i 7.6 virtual machine from the Certified PowerVS Base VMs collection, which takes 30 to 60 minutes to provision
  • The two Flight400 distribution files, FLGHT400.FILE and Install-Flight400.sql, downloaded from the links in the Setup chapter
  • A local folder is available to serve as your Bob project workspace, and an SSH client is installed (macOS, Linux and Windows 10 or later include one)

MANAGING CONSUMPTION OF BOBCOINS

The Premium Package requires agentic AI capabilities, which consume Bob Resource Units (Bobcoins). The architecture overview in Module 1 and the RPG modernization in Module 2 are the most expensive prompts in this lab. The AGENTS member and the Understand scan exist to lower that cost: once they are in place, Bob answers structural questions from metadata instead of re-reading source members. Finish each module's prompts before you experiment with the optional variations.

The work proceeds in six stages:

  • Request the Premium Package for i entitlement through the route that matches your job role, then confirm it has landed in your Bob account
  • Install the IBM Bob Premium Package for i extension and the IBM i Development Pack from the Extensions view
  • Reserve an IBM i 7.6 virtual machine from IBM Technology Zone and download the Flight400 distribution files
  • Create a local project workspace and connect Bob to the partition over SSH
  • Have Bob install tn5250 on the partition so that a 5250 terminal opens inside the IDE
  • Upload the Flight400 save file to the IFS, restore it into the FLGHT400 library and add that library to your library list

Afterwards, you will be ready to begin Module 1 | Analyze.

docs.title: ii. Request entitlements to Bob Premium Package for i
docs.text:
THIS LAB REQUIRES THE PREMIUM PACKAGE FOR i

Without the IBM Bob Premium Package for i (PPi) entitlement, IBM Bob can still open and read RPG, CL and DDS source, but the IBM i Developer and IBM i Database modes and the specifically-trained capabilities that the package provides will be unavailable. If neither mode appears in your Agentic Sidebar by the end of this chapter, the entitlement has not been linked to your Bob account.

Before Bob can operate against IBM i, you will want to request license entitlements to IBM Bob Premium Package for i (PPi). The pathway for doing so differs depending on your role as either an IBM regular employee or a business partner.

Without such entitlements, IBM Bob will still attempt to work with IBM i and RPG application code, though without the specifically-trained models and capabilities that PPi offers. For example, if your Agentic Sidebar shows no IBM i Developer mode in its mode selector, that indicates that your IBM Bob account has not been linked to the PPi entitlement.

Select from one of the two options below, according to your job role, to register for IBM Bob Premium Package for i entitlements:

IBM REGULAR EMPLOYEES

Request access via the following link: https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/bob/addons

Once registered, IBM Bob Premium Package for i capabilities will automatically be authorized and connected to your IBM Bob account. No additional configuration or PPi-specific logins are required.

BUSINESS PARTNERS

  1. Requests for PPi licensing entitlements can be made via IBM Technology Zone. Visit the following collection to begin the process:

    URL: https://techzone.ibm.com/collection/bob-business-partner-enablement/environments

    From the left-hand side of the page, click the Environments tab.

  1. Four options will be available:

    • Request entitlement for IBM Bob Enterprise
    • Request entitlement for IBM Bob Premium Package for i
    • Request entitlement for IBM Bob Premium Package for Z
    • Request entitlement for IBM Bob Premium Package for Java

    Click the Reserve it button below the Request entitlement for IBM Bob Premium Package for i tile.

  1. Step 1: General of the configuration process will ask you to specify a Name and Description for your reservation. When ready, click Next in the bottom-right corner to continue.

  1. Step 2: Business purpose must be set to Learning in order to bypass the need for an opportunity number. If you mistakenly click the wrong option, or if the reservation system does not allow you to continue without an opportunity number, exit out from this page and try again. When ready, click Next to continue.

  1. Step 3: Deployment will ask you to specify the Geography for your deployment. Select the data center location that is closest to you. When ready, click Next to continue.

  1. Step 4: Scheduling will ask you to specify the go-live and termination dates for your deployment. Note that deployments can only be scheduled up to 12 hours of run-time before the instance is automatically deprovisioned. This is sufficient time to complete the hands-on lab materials. If you need additional time, you can provision a new instance using the same instructions provided within this lab guide. When ready, click Next to continue.

  1. Step 5: Configure can be left blank (default state of "There is nothing to configure here.") When ready, click Next to continue.

  1. Step 6: Review and submit will ask you to review your configuration settings before submitting the request. Scroll down through your reservation details and, if you approve, check the I agree to IBM Technology Zone's terms & conditions and user security policies. box at the bottom of the page. When ready, click Submit to initiate the reservation request.

  1. The web browser will redirect automatically to IBM Technology Zone's My requests dashboard. From this page, you can monitor and track the progression of your reservation request as it moves from Scheduled to Provisioning to Ready. Wait until the request is marked as Ready before advancing.

    Average deployment times are roughly 5 minutes or less.

  1. When the reservation is Ready, you will receive an email to your inbox providing you with a link to the environment and the same details will also be accessible via the My requests dashboard (where you were tracking the reservation request).

    Click either the View your request link in the email body OR click the arrow to the left of your reservation name on the My requests dashboard to expand details about the request.

  1. Both links will direct to the IBM Bob dashboard:

    URL: https://bob.ibm.com/admin

    Authenticate and log in using your IBM ID, which (since you should have previously registered for IBM Bob) will automatically be associated with your Bob account.

  1. The web browser will redirect to a welcome splash screen reading "Welcome [your username]!" where you are prompted to Choose workspace.

    Depending on how you previously registered for general access to IBM Bob, the default option below this may display text such as IBM Internal or Free Trial (or potentially something else).

    • Click the box below Choose workspace to open a drop-down menu
    • Your request via IBM Technology Zone for PPi entitlements will have added a new option to this list, similar to TECHZONE-BobathonV2 (us-east). This entry is the PPi licensing entitlement that IBM Technology Zone provisioned for you
    • Select the TECHZONE-BobathonV2 ... option as your workspace and then continue with the login

  1. The web browser will automatically load into the IBM Bob dashboard.

    • Verify in the top-left corner that TECHZONE-BobathonV2 ... is selected for Organization
    • Click the Subscription tab to view details about your subscription, plan type, seats, and Bobcoins
    • Towards the bottom of the panel, under the Premium packages section, there will be an IBM i tile marked as Active: this confirms your IBM Bob account is now successfully linked (and entitled for use) with the IBM Technology Zone Premium Package for i license.

docs.title: iii. Install and authorize Bob Premium Package for i
docs.text:
With your entitlements connected to your IBM Bob account, you will next need to install the IBM Bob Premium Package for i extension within the Bob IDE. The extension adds IBM i-specific modes, tools, skills, workflows and slash commands to the capabilities already present within Bob. Every module of this lab uses them.

  1. In IBM Bob IDE, open the Extensions view (Cmd+Shift+X / Ctrl+Shift+X) and search for Premium Package.

    Locate the IBM Bob Premium Package for i tile (publisher: IBM) and click Install.

  1. A "Do you trust the publisher 'IBM' and 2 others?" dialog appears. Review the details, then click Trust Publishers & Install to proceed.

    Installation of the Premium Package and its bundled dependencies (including Code for IBM i) will complete in a few seconds.

  1. After the extension has installed, look towards the bottom-right corner of the Bob IDE interface. Along the bottom edge of the interface there will be an interactable button labelled Bob Settings — click this button to open the Settings panel.

  1. From the Settings panel, make sure the General tab (left side) is the one being displayed.

    • Locate the Team setting, which by default at this stage might be set to either IBM Internal, Trial, or some other variation
    • Click the name of your Team to pull open a drop-down menu
    • Select the TECHZONE-BobathonV2 ... option to connect to your Premium Package entitlements

  1. Afterwards, further down the panel adjacent the Add ons setting, you should now see the IBM Bob Premium Package for i displayed.

    • Look further to the right of this setting to locate the Install button
    • Click Install to initiate an Install addon operation (this might seem redundant but it is a required activation within Settings to fully connect the Premium Package)
    • Wait a moment for a pop-up notification to appear in the bottom-right corner of the Bob IDE interface, similar to the one shown in the screenshot below
    • Bob IDE might request an application restart to implement the changes; if this is the case, accept and restart the IDE

  1. At this stage, the Premium Package should both be fully authorized with your IBM Bob account and integrated with your Bob IDE. To verify, open the Agentic Sidebar and click the Agent modes selector button.

    Within the drop-down menu of Agent modes, you should now see IBM Bob Premium Package-specific modes that were previously unavailable: IBM i Developer and IBM i Database.

docs.title: iv. Install the IBM i Development Pack
docs.text:
The Premium Package bundles Code for IBM i, which is enough to browse objects and edit source. The later modules lean on companion extensions from the Code for IBM i ecosystem as well: Module 4 drives RPGUnit through the IBM i Testing extension, and the Db2 for IBM i extension gives you a place to run SQL statements yourself alongside the work of Module 3. Depending on the release of the Premium Package, some of these may already be present on your machine. The IBM i Development Pack is an extension pack maintained by the Code for IBM i team. It installs whichever are missing in one pass, together with the RPGLE, CL and COBOL language tooling and the display-file renderer.

  1. In the Extensions view, search for IBM i Development Pack.

    Locate the IBM i Development Pack tile (publisher: HalcyonTechLtd, the Code for IBM i team) and click Install. The pack installs its member extensions in one pass; the count varies by release, so expect a dozen or so new entries under Installed when it finishes.

    ALREADY INSTALLED?

    If the tile already shows Uninstall instead of Install, the pack arrived with an earlier Code for IBM i installation on this machine and there is nothing further to do.

  1. If the Bob IDE prompts for a Reload (or a Restart Extensions notification appears in the bottom-right corner), accept it. The language tooling and the IBM i Testing view register on the next activation.

    Afterwards, search the Extensions view for IBM i Testing and confirm that it appears under Installed. That extension is the one Module 4 checks for before it installs RPGUnit on the partition.

docs.title: v. Reserve the IBM i 7.6 virtual machine
docs.text:
APPROVAL & PROVISIONING TIME

Once submitted, the request typically moves from Scheduled → Provisioning → Ready over the course of roughly 30–60 minutes. You will receive an email notification once the environment is fully deployed and available for use.

Before installing the Flight400 demo app, you will need an IBM i environment provisioned through IBM Technology Zone. The steps below walk you through requesting a Certified PowerVS Base VM running IBM i 7.6, which you will use throughout the remainder of the lab.

  1. Begin by signing in with your IBMid on the IBM login page.

    Enter your IBMid in the field, press Continue, then complete the password prompt on the subsequent page.

  1. Open the Certified PowerVS Base VMs collection in IBM Technology Zone.

    Locate the IBM i 7.6 IBM Cloud PowerVS VSI tile and click the ibmcloud-2 environment button at the bottom of the tile.

  1. On Step 1: General, fill in the request details.

    • Name: IBM i Modernization with Bob
    • Description: Hands-on labs to learn IBM i modernization using IBM Bob AI assistant

    Then press Next.

  1. On Step 2: Business purpose, select Learning as the primary use.

    Leave the Opportunity fields blank and press Next to continue.

  1. On Step 3: Deployment, confirm the pre-selected geography:

    itz-shared-power - americas - us-east region - wdc07 datacenter

    Press Next to continue.

  1. On Step 4: Scheduling, review the default Start date and End date. The environment can be reserved for up to 12 hours per request.

    Adjust the dates if needed, then press Next.

  1. On Step 5: Configuration, review the default VM specs:

    Setting Value CPU 0.5 Memory 4 GB Boot volume 50 GB Secondary disk None Network interface Public

    These defaults are sufficient for the lab. Press Review.

  1. On Step 6: Review and submit, verify all details, then tick the checkbox to agree to IBM Technology Zone's terms & conditions and user security policies.

    Press Submit.

  1. You will land on a Success confirmation page displaying your Request ID — save this for reference.

    Press Track my request to monitor the provisioning status.

  1. On the My requests page, you will see your newly submitted IBM i Modernization with Bob request with a Scheduled status.

    The environment will progress through Scheduled → Provisioning → Ready automatically. You can leave this page and return later — an email will notify you when it's ready.

  1. Once the status changes to Ready, return to the request page and click the expand arrow (the V icon) to the left of the environment name to reveal the connection details.

  1. Within the expanded Outputs panel, capture the following — you will need them to SSH into your IBM i VM in the next section:

    • Deployment user name
    • Virtual machine 1 public IP address
    • Deployment SSH private key — click Download and store the key file securely

docs.title: vi. Download the lab assets
docs.text:
While your IBM i environment provisions, download the Flight400 distribution — the single, production-style application that every module in this lab builds upon.

  1. Download the Flight400 project files from the links below and save them to your computer:

    • FLIGHT400.FILE
    • Install-Flight400.sql
  1. Keep both files somewhere convenient for the time being, as the next section will have you create the workspace folder they will reside in (alongside the SSH key you downloaded from IBM Technology Zone.)

docs.title: vii. Set up the Project workspace
docs.text:
PREREQUISITES

You should have the following in place before starting this section:

  • IBM Bob IDE — installed and authenticated (from your registration path)
  • ssh_private_key.pem — downloaded from IBM Technology Zone (section v)
  • FLGHT400.FILE and Install-Flight400.sql — downloaded from the Flight400 distribution package (section vi)

With your IBM i environment provisioned and the Deployment SSH private key downloaded, the next step is to prepare a local workspace, open it in IBM Bob IDE, and lock down permissions on the SSH key so it can be used for authentication.

  1. On your laptop, create a local folder — for example ~/ibmiflight400 — and move the three files into it: FLGHT400.FILE, Install-Flight400.sql, and ssh_private_key.pem.

    Confirm all three files appear side-by-side in the folder before continuing.

  1. Open IBM Bob IDE. In the Explorer view, click Open Folder to open your local workspace.

  1. In the file dialog, navigate to the folder you just created (ibmiflight400), select it, and press Open.

    Bob IDE will now treat this folder as your workspace for the remainder of the lab.

  1. From the top menu bar, select Terminal → New Terminal to open an integrated terminal at the root of your workspace.

  1. In the terminal, tighten the permissions on the SSH private key so it can be used for authentication. Copy and paste the following command, then press Enter:

    chmod 600 ssh_private_key.pem

    SSH will refuse to use a private key that is readable by other users on the system. chmod 600 restricts read and write access to only your user account, satisfying SSH's security check.

docs.title: viii. Connect to the IBM i LPAR
docs.text:
With the IBM Bob Premium Package for i extension now installed, you can next point Bob to your provisioned IBM i LPAR using the connection details captured earlier.

  1. On the IBM Bob Premium Package for i welcome page, click Connect to an IBM i.

  1. In the IBM i Login form, fill in the connection details:

    • Connection Name: IBM i Modernization
    • Host or IP Address: the Virtual machine 1 public IP address from section v
    • Port (SSH): 22 (default)
    • Username: ITZUSER

    Leave the Password field empty — authentication will use the SSH private key instead.

  1. Scroll down to the Private Key section and click Select File.

    In the file picker, navigate to your workspace folder, select ssh_private_key.pem, and press Open.

  1. Confirm the Private Key path is now populated in the login form, then press Connect at the bottom of the form.

  1. A Directory permissions dialog may appear — "Security recommendation: Update directory permissions?" — asking to create /home/ITZUSER/.vscode with permissions 700.

    Click Yes to accept the recommendation.

  1. Once connected, the IBM i sidebar populates with User Library List (QGPL, QTEMP), Object Browser, and IFS Browser entries. This is confirmation that Bob is talking to your LPAR.

    Dismiss the transient notifications on the right (SQL job, local actions, deploy directory prompts) and close the welcome tab.

docs.title: ix. Enable the 5250 terminal
docs.text:
Certified PowerVS Base VMs ship without the tn5250 package installed, so a 5250 terminal session from Bob IDE will initially fail. Rather than SSH-ing in and installing it by hand, you will ask Bob itself to install tn5250 on the LPAR. The rest of the lab uses Bob in the same way.

  1. Open the Bob chat panel. At the bottom of the chat, expand the mode selector and choose IBM i Developer.

    This mode gives Bob the tools and skills needed to run CL commands, install PASE packages, and edit your user profile on the LPAR.

  1. Click into the prompt field and paste the following request (press Cmd+V or alternatively Ctrl+V):

    I'm getting the error "5250 terminal is not supported. Please install tn5250 via yum on the remote system." in the Code for IBM i VS Code extension. Please install tn5250 on my remote IBM i system, make sure it's in the default PATH, and set up my user profile so it's available in login shells. After that, tell me to reconnect using "Connect and Reload Server Settings" in VS Code.

    Press Enter to execute the instruction.

  1. Bob will perform the yum install tn5250-0.17.6-1 request to update /home/ITZUSER/.profile and /QOpenSys/etc/profile.local — such that /QOpenSys/pkgs/bin is on the PATH for every login shell used after the fact.

    When Bob finishes, click the disconnect button highlighted in the bottom-left status bar to close the current session with your LPAR.

  1. In the IBM i sidebar, right-click your server (IBM i Modernization) and choose Connect and Reload Server Settings.

    This forces the extension to re-read the remote environment — including the updated PATH — so that the tn5250 binary Bob just installed is picked up.

  1. Within the Bob IDE status bar (bottom of the window), hover over the gear icon to reveal the connection pop-up.

    From the options presented, click Terminals to open a new Terminal console session on the LPAR.

  1. When prompted "Select a terminal type", choose 5250.

    The PASE option gives you a Unix-style shell on the LPAR — useful for running yum, editing files, and inspecting IFS content. The 5250 option gives you the classic green-screen IBM i session used by RPG applications like FLIGHT400. Module 6 relies on the PASE side as well, since that is where Node.js runs.

  1. A new IBM i 5250: IBM i Modernization tab opens, showing the classic Sign On screen — System, Subsystem, Display, and User fields ready for input.

    You now have a working 5250 terminal directly inside Bob IDE, alongside a PASE shell in the bottom panel.

docs.title: x. Uploading the Flight400 files to the IFS
docs.text:
Bob is now connected to your LPAR, but the Flight400 save file and install script still live only on your laptop. Use Bob IDE's Deploy Selected Files feature to push them into the IFS on your LPAR, where the install script can be executed.

  1. From the Activity Bar tabs along the left side of the Bob IDE, click the Explorer icon to switch back to your local workspace view.

    You should see FLGHT400.FILE and Install-Flight400.sql at the top of the tree.

  1. Select both FLGHT400.FILE and Install-Flight400.sql (hold Cmd / Ctrl and click each file), then right-click the selection and choose Deploy Selected Files.

  1. On the first deploy, a notification will appear in the bottom-right: "Chosen location … is not configured for deployment."

    • Click Set deploy location to configure the target IFS directory
    • Accept the suggested path (typically /home/ITZUSER/builds/ibmiflight400)
    • This becomes the IFS directory that mirrors your local workspace

  1. In the Activity Bar, click the IBM i icon to switch to the IBM i sidebar, where you can browse the LPAR.

  1. Click the refresh icon on the IFS Browser header to reload the tree so the newly deployed files show up.

  1. Expand /home/ITZUSER → builds → ibmiflight400.

    Confirm that both FLGHT400.FILE and Install-Flight400.sql are now present on the LPAR.

docs.title: xi. Restoring the FLGHT400 library
docs.text:
With the save file staged in the IFS, the next step is to run the SQL install script. The script uses IBM i services to create a save file object in QSYS, copy the IFS save file into it, and restore the library. Before running it, you will point the script at the exact IFS path Bob just deployed.

  1. In the IFS Browser, right-click FLGHT400.FILE and choose Copy Path. You will paste this into the install script in a moment.

  1. Switch back to the Explorer view via the Activity Bar.

  1. Open Install-Flight400.sql in the editor and locate the three configuration variables near the top of the BEGIN block:

    DECLARE v_ifs_path  VARCHAR(256) DEFAULT '/home/BENOIT/builds/…';
DECLARE v_rst_lib   VARCHAR(10)  DEFAULT 'FLGHT400';   -- target library
DECLARE v_owner     VARCHAR(10)  DEFAULT NULL;         -- set to a profile …

  1. Replace the default v_ifs_path string with the path you copied in step 1.

    • The new string should look like /home/ITZUSER/builds/ibmiflight400/FLGHT400.FILE
    • Leave v_rst_lib as FLGHT400 and v_owner as NULL
    • Save the file (Cmd+S / Ctrl+S) and then close the editor tab

  1. Switch back to the IBM i sidebar and locate Install-Flight400.sql in the IFS Browser under /home/ITZUSER/builds/ibmiflight400.

    Because you edited the file locally, redeploy it (right-click → Deploy Selected Files) so the LPAR has the updated version before running it. If the IFS copy is out of date, the script will use the wrong path.

  1. Right-click Install-Flight400.sql in the IFS Browser and choose Run Action….

  1. From the action selector at the top of the window, choose Run SQL Statements (RUNSQLSTM).

  1. The integrated terminal will open and display the RUNSQLSTM output. Wait for the message summary to show 0 level severity errors found in source, followed by ***** END OF LISTING *****.

    The FLGHT400 library — programs, source members, and database files — is now restored on your LPAR.

docs.title: xii. Adding FLGHT400 to your library list
docs.text:
The library exists on the LPAR, but Bob won't find its objects by default. IBM i only searches libraries that appear in your library list. Add FLGHT400 to your list so every subsequent lookup, filter, and Bob prompt can reach the application.

  1. In the IBM i sidebar, hover over the User Library List header and click the + (Add library) icon.

  1. In the prompt at the top of the window ("Library to add"), type FLGHT400.

  1. Press Enter to confirm. FLGHT400 (*PROD) now appears in your User Library List alongside QGPL and QTEMP.

docs.title: xiii. You're ready to proceed
docs.text:
Setup is complete if:

  • IBM Bob is authenticated and the Add ons setting lists IBM Bob Premium Package for i
  • The Agentic Sidebar's mode selector lists IBM i Developer and IBM i Database alongside Agent, Plan and Ask
  • The Extensions view lists the IBM i Development Pack and its member extensions (among them IBM i Testing) under Installed
  • The IBM i LPAR is provisioned and Bob is connected to it as ITZUSER
  • Both PASE and 5250 terminals are working from inside the IDE
  • The FLGHT400 library is restored and appears in your User Library List alongside QGPL and QTEMP

You are ready to begin the hands-on work.

Onward to Module 1 | Analyze. You will begin by exploring FLIGHT400 in the Object Browser and writing Bob's AGENTS member with /init. You will then scan the application into the Understand Dashboard and produce an architecture overview and an entity relationship diagram from the live system. Each later module builds on the documentation and the scan you produce there.
